findings.location: docs/feature/ui-bare-pages/architecture.md:382 (Constraints, DEVIATION from P4's wording); brief.md P4 and Decisions
findings.obligation: The design must agree with the current confirmed authority. The user decided 2026-11-21 that the claim password is new-password, and P4 was reworded to match.
findings.observation: architecture.md:382 still states a DEVIATION from P4's wording, says P4 calls the claim field the current password, and asks the owner to rule. brief.md P4 no longer says that. The record shows a deviation that does not exist and an open owner question that the user closed.
findings.remediation: Remove or reword the DEVIATION constraint so it records the decision as made: the claim password takes new-password per P4 and the 2026-11-21 user decision. Keep the autocomplete law at architecture.md:1440 unchanged.

findings.location: docs/product/architecture/ADR-002.md Decision and Consequences; architecture.md:336 and :402 (show_keyboard_help)
findings.obligation: One URL that answers two different bodies by a request header must name its cache contract, so a cache or the back-forward cache cannot hand the fragment to a navigation or the framed document to the overlay fetch.
findings.observation: ADR-002 and the design say nothing about Vary or Cache-Control for GET /keyboard-help. Shipped dynamic responses carry no Vary (grep of crates/foundry-app/src finds none; the Cache-Control middleware at lib.rs:311 only stamps /static). A cache keyed on URL alone can serve the fragment to a navigation (the unstyled page returns) or the document to keyboard.js:323 (nested html in the host). The Quint model has only the four destinations and cannot see this.
findings.remediation: Add to ADR-002 and the show_keyboard_help target: both arms send Vary: Sec-Fetch-Dest (or Cache-Control: no-store on both), and add one oracle read that the header is present on both arms.

findings.location: docs/feature/ui-bare-pages/architecture.md:142, :416 and :1760-1775 (signed-in arm of show_keyboard_help); ADR-BARE-PAGES-002 Decision
findings.obligation: The signed-in arm must match the nav of other pages and add no nav rule. The shipped home_for needs a csrf token, the instance-admin flag and the workspace id, and the rail footer sign-out form needs a cookie-matched token.
findings.observation: The design names only 'the shipped neutral home-for constructor'. It does not say where csrf, is_instance_admin and workspace_id come from, nor that the page arm must mint the csrf cookie with ensure_csrf_cookie and send the Set-Cookie (projects.rs:84-101 does). A page that calls home_for with a token it did not set draws a sign-out form that fails the double-submit check. No case reads the rail on the signed-in arm: the four cases at :1766-1782 read only headers and frame choice.
findings.remediation: State in ADR-002-amendment/architecture the three inputs and the csrf mint with its Set-Cookie on the signed-in page arm (still no-store). Add finite cases: signed-in page shows the rail with exactly one primary member marked, the sign-out form token equals the csrf cookie, and a session whose user no longer resolves answers the card.

findings.obligation: The new stylesheet blocks must keep the shipped canzan-theme-system laws: text pairs reach 4.5 to 1 in both palettes, and a chip sits on an opaque surface (canzan-theme-system.feature:168, :246).
findings.observation: The new cases require only that the chip resolves a background, a border and a radius and that the file-selector button resolves the muted border and unfilled background. None reads a contrast ratio or opaqueness in the dark and light palettes. A translucent chip tint or a low-contrast chip or button text would pass every listed case and fail the shipped law at its next run.
findings.remediation: Add to the two cases: the chip text and the file-selector-button text each reach at least 4.5 to 1 against the surface behind them, and the chip background is opaque, read in both palettes; name the existing opaque tokens the blocks use.

observations.text: Round 4 read. Finding 4 resolved: L5 (architecture.md:1700, :1704) names the opaque --cz-bg-2 chip pairing and the --cz-surface/--cz-muted/--cz-text button pairing with 4.5 to 1 in both palettes; all five tokens exist in the shipped stylesheet in both palettes (foundry.*.css:84-98, :190-197) and the keycap rule uses --cz-bg-2 and --cz-line.
